title: Conversational Runtime Packaging and Rollout Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the productization, packaging, and phased rollout plan for Redwood's conversational LLM runtime packaging options. It is intended for product, engineering (serving runtime & private deployments), go-to-market, and customer success teams preparing for the Feature Launch (internal codename: Project Hummingbird).

Goals and success metrics

- Primary goals:
  - Ship a reusable packaging bundle that allows customers to select a conversational runtime profile (hosted, dedicated, private) with pre-defined fidelity/cost tradeoffs.
  - Make onboarding for PLG customers possible in < 20 minutes for hosted and < 2 weeks for Dedicated proof-of-concept.
  - Provide migration paths for enterprise customers to move from hosted to Private with minimal behavioral drift.

- Success metrics (first 90 days):
  - 50 production tenants adopt a packaged conversational profile.
  - Median first-byte latency for hosted conversational endpoints <= 120ms for 1k tokens.
  - 10% reduction in average tokens-per-request cost for customers that adopt recommended caching/batching profiles.

Target segments and personas

1) Developer-led startups: want a quick, documented package (hosted runtime + example prompts + SDK guides).
2) Mid-market product teams: need Dedicated bundles that include capacity guidance, SLAs, and a migration checklist.
3) Regulated enterprises: require Private deployment packaging (VPC/KMS integrations, encrypted logs, audit hooks).

Product requirements (must):

1. Packaging profiles: each profile is a named bundle ("conversational-lite", "conversational-balanced", "conversational-high-fidelity") that includes: model variant, quantization profile, batching defaults, KV-cache policy, and recommended SLO targets.
2. Configuration schema: a single human-readable YAML manifest that operators and customers can use to instantiate the runtime.
3. SDK & quickstarts: language SDK examples for Python/Node + a one-click Hosted playground for the lite profile.
4. Observability contract: per-profile dashboards, token breakdowns, and failure mode counters.
5. Migration playbook: a prescriptive checklist and smoke tests for moving between profiles and deployments.

Non-functional requirements:

- Packaging size: Private appliance bundle <= 12 GB compressed (base image + model weights overlays excluded).
- Cold-start target: average cold-start <= 18s for Private short-lifetime containers with warm-up sequence.
- Compatibility: all profiles must support the function-calling surface and structured output hooks.

Design specification (high-level)

Components:

- Packaging Manifest (YAML): defines profile metadata, resource hints, model pin, quantization spec, and observability hooks.
- Profile Registry Service: internal catalog mapping profile name -> runtime recipe + compatibility matrix. Owned by eng-platform.
- Runtime adapter layer: small shim in serving runtime that ingests the manifest and applies runtime flags (batching windows, KV cache TTLs, kernel preferences). Owned by eng-serving-runtime.
- Migration operator: CLI and Console flow for swapping profiles with canary / traffic-splitting support.

Example packaging manifest (YAML)

```yaml
profile: conversational-balanced
model: mix-redwood-3b-v2
quantization: q4_f16
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  preferred_latency_ms: 120
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  ttl_seconds: 1200
observability:
  metrics: [latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hits]
  traces: sample_rate: 0.05
```

Compatibility matrix (text table)

| Profile | Hosted | Dedicated | Private (VPC) | Minimum GPU | Notes |
| conversational-lite | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1xA10G | Fast cold-start, lower quality |
| conversational-balanced | Yes | Yes | Yes | 1xA100 | Default for most customers |
| conversational-high-fidelity | No | Yes | Yes | 2xH100 | Requires reserve capacity, higher cost |

API surface and examples

- The runtime must accept the standard Redwood generation/chat API with a new "profile" param. Example cURL:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"mix-redwood-3b-v2","profile":"conversational-balanced","input":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'

Roadmap and phased rollout

Phase 0 (Q2 2028): Internal validation
- Implement manifest reader in runtime (eng-serving-runtime).
- Build Profile Registry and seed three canonical profiles.
- Internal docs and sample manifests.

Phase 1 (Q3 2028): Private & Dedicated pilot
- Launch Dedicated pilot with 5 customers and run load tests.
- Private packaged appliance image published for 2 early enterprise customers.
- Add Console UX flow for selecting profiles and viewing recommended capacity.

Phase 2 (Q4 2028): Hosted public release (lite + balanced)
- Publish hosted "conversational-lite" and "conversational-balanced" profiles.
- Quickstart templates in SDKs and Console.
- Launch product marketing collateral and pricing tiers.

Phase 3 (Q1 2029): Fidelity and scale
- Add "conversational-high-fidelity" for dedicated/enterprise customers.
- Automated migration assistant and A/B evaluation harnesses for quality regression checks.

Pricing and packaging notes

Pricing principles:
- Keep per-token pricing transparent; profiles adjust per-token compute multiplier.
- Offer reserved capacity multipliers for Dedicated with committed discounts.
- Provide a free hosting tier for "conversational-lite" up to a small monthly token cap to drive PLG adoption.

Suggested pricing table (internal):

| Profile | Hosted (per 1k tokens) | Dedicated (base per 1k tokens) | Reserved commit discount |
| conversational-lite | $0.30 | $0.25 | 15% for 12-month commit |
| conversational-balanced | $0.80 | $0.60 | 25% for 12-month commit |
| conversational-high-fidelity | N/A | $2.40 | 30% for 12-month commit + capacity surcharge |

Billing notes:
- For Dedicated, a combined model: hourly reserved node + per-token usage for overflow.
- For Private, we provide a metering agent that reports per-profile usage; billing for Private is invoiced via the enterprise contract.

Release notes (initial public release items)

- Feature: Profile manifest support in runtime and SDKs.
- Feature: Profile Registry + Console selection.
- Feature: Hosted delivery for conversational-lite and conversational-balanced.
- Improvement: Default batching heuristics adjusted for conversational workloads.
- Known limitations: conversational-high-fidelity not yet available on Hosted; cold-start for Private large-image still depends on customer infra.

Rollout checklist (owners & steps)

| Step | Owner | Due | Status |
| Finalize manifest schema | eng-platform | 2028-06-15 | in_progress |
| Implement manifest hooks in runtime | eng-serving-runtime | 2028-07-01 | in_progress |
| Console UX for profile picker | eng-platform | 2028-07-15 | planned |
| Billing mapping and SKU creation | finance-legal | 2028-07-20 | planned |
| Pilot onboarding (Dedicated) | customer-success | 2028-08-01 | planned |

Monitoring and observability requirements

- Per-profile dashboards must expose: 95th/99th latency, tokens-in/out, cache hit ratio, batch sizes distribution, and quality regressions (via eval capture).
- Alerting thresholds (initial):
  - p95 latency > 200ms for balanced profile => page on-call SRE.
  - cache hit ratio < 30% for balanced profile => ticket to runtime team.
  - regression alert: automated eval delta > 2% in top-1 correctness => alert to applied-ml.

Migration and rollback patterns

1. Canary: route 5% traffic to new profile for 24 hours; monitor latency, cost, and eval capture.
2. Expand to 25% after green signals for 48 hours.
3. Full switch with immediate rollback flag preserved for 1 hour.

Security, compliance, and data handling notes

- Private packaging must include a hardened default: logs redaction enabled, KMS integration for keys, and an audit collector with immutable storage.
- Sensitive telemetry: token-level usage is hashed and aggregated for hosted telemetry pipelines.

Open decisions and risks

- Decision needed: exact per-token multipliers for balanced/high-fidelity profiles (pricing team).
- Risk: model variant compatibility may block a profile on certain hardware (mitigation: automated compatibility checks in Profile Registry).

Appendix: example Console flow and CLI commands

- CLI: create a profile override for a tenant

redwood profile apply --tenant tenant-123 --profile conversational-balanced --manifest ./manifests/balanced.yaml

- Console steps:
  1. Tenant -> Settings -> Runtime Profiles
  2. Select "conversational-balanced"
  3. Preview capacity recommendation -> Confirm -> Apply
